paragraphs.title: Choosing Faith Instead of Envy and Anger

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious.”
easy.q: Whom should we not envy?

easy.explanation: Verse 3 commands, “Trust in the LORD, and do good.”
easy.q: In whom should we trust?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “Cease from anger, and forsake wrath.”
easy.q: What should we do instead of being angry?

medium.explanation: They will be cut down like grass and wither like green herb.
medium.q: Why should we not envy evildoers?

medium.explanation: The verse joins these commands: “Trust in the LORD, and do good.”
medium.q: What accompanies trusting in the LORD?

medium.explanation: Verse 7 connects resting in the LORD with waiting patiently for Him.
medium.q: What does “rest in the LORD” mean in this passage?

answers: Trust and good works versus envy and anger
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts trusting God and doing good with fretting, envy, and wrath.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in verses 1–8?

challenge.explanation: Righteousness will come forth “as the light,” and judgment as the noonday.
challenge.q: What does the image of light teach about righteousness?

challenge.explanation: The psalm says not to fret because of the man who prospers in his wicked way.
challenge.q: What response is rejected toward one who prospers wickedly?

paragraphs.title: The Disappearance of the Wicked and Inheritance of the Land

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “Evildoers shall be cut off.”
easy.q: What will happen to evildoers?

answers: Those that wait upon the LORD
easy.explanation: Those who wait upon the LORD shall inherit the earth.
easy.q: Who shall inherit the earth?

easy.explanation: The meek shall inherit the earth and delight in the abundance of peace.
easy.q: What shall the meek enjoy?

medium.explanation: Verse 9 directly promises them an inheritance of the earth.
medium.q: What is promised to those who wait upon the LORD?

answers: They will soon not be found
medium.explanation: Verse 10 says, “Yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be.”
medium.q: How is the future of the wicked described?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes the removal and end of evildoers.
medium.q: What does “cut off” mean in this context?

answers: The wicked seem present, but soon will not be found
The meek disappear while the wicked remain
challenge.explanation: The psalm says the wicked may be observed now, but afterward they will not be.
challenge.q: What change is described between the present and the future?

answers: They are connected with inheriting the earth
challenge.explanation: Both groups are promised the inheritance of the earth.
challenge.q: What do those who wait upon the LORD and the meek have in common?

answers: The meek inherit and delight in abundant peace
challenge.explanation: The meek inherit the earth and delight in the abundance of peace.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between inheritance and peace?

paragraphs.title: The Wicked's Schemes Turning Against Them

easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “The wicked plotteth against the just.”
easy.q: Against whom does the wicked man plot?

easy.explanation: They draw the sword and bend the bow against the poor and needy.
easy.q: Against whom do the wicked draw their weapons?

answers: The sword will enter their heart and the bows will break
easy.explanation: Their violence turns back upon them.
easy.q: What will happen to their weapons?

answers: He sees that their day is coming
medium.explanation: Verse 13 says the Lord laughs because He sees that the wicked man's day is coming.
medium.q: Why does the Lord laugh at the wicked?

answers: The weapons pass to the just
medium.explanation: Their sword enters their own heart, and their bows are broken.
medium.q: What does the turning of the weapons signify?

medium.explanation: Gnashing the teeth shows hatred and hostility toward the just.
medium.q: What does gnashing with the teeth express?

answers: Violent schemes return upon their planner
challenge.explanation: The weapons prepared for others turn against the wicked themselves.
challenge.q: What principle of justice appears in these verses?

answers: Their end is hidden from Him
He sees the day of their downfall
He takes no notice of them
challenge.explanation: The Lord sees that the wicked man's day is coming.
challenge.q: What does the verse emphasize about God's knowledge of the wicked?

answers: The wicked gives, the just takes, and the poor wins
The just plots and the wicked escapes
The wicked plots, the Lord sees, and the weapons break
challenge.explanation: This is the progression presented in verses 12–15.
challenge.q: What is the sequence of events in the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Person's Advantage and God's Support

answers: A little that a righteous man has
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “A little that a righteous man hath is better.”
easy.q: What is better than the riches of many wicked?

easy.explanation: Verse 17 says, “The arms of the wicked shall be broken.”
easy.q: What will happen to the arms of the wicked?

easy.explanation: The LORD upholds the righteous.
easy.q: Who upholds the righteous?

medium.explanation: The wicked's power breaks, but the LORD upholds the righteous.
medium.q: Why is a little possessed by the righteous better than much wealth?

medium.explanation: They shall not be ashamed in the evil time.
medium.q: What is promised to the upright in evil times?

medium.explanation: The enemies of the LORD shall consume away into smoke.
medium.q: What happens to the enemies of the LORD?

answers: The amount of wealth does not determine true advantage
Only great riches count as success
The wicked are always better off
challenge.explanation: A little belonging to the righteous is better than the riches of many wicked.
challenge.q: What view of success do these verses present?

answers: His knowledge leads to their loss
Their inheritance shall be for ever
challenge.explanation: The LORD knows their days, and their inheritance shall be for ever.
challenge.q: What connection is made between the LORD knowing the upright and their inheritance?

answers: The righteous disappear and the wicked remain
Both groups disappear in the same way
The righteous are upheld while the wicked perish
challenge.explanation: The LORD upholds the righteous, while the wicked and His enemies consume away.
challenge.q: What contrast appears at the end of the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Way: Giving, Blessing and Stability

easy.explanation: The righteous “sheweth mercy, and giveth.”
easy.q: What does the righteous person do for others?

easy.explanation: Verse 23 says, “The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD.”
easy.q: Who orders the steps of a good man?

answers: He will not be utterly cast down
easy.explanation: The LORD upholds him with His hand.
easy.q: What will not happen to the righteous person when he falls?

answers: The wicked borrow without repaying, while the righteous give and lend
The wicked give while the righteous take
medium.explanation: The wicked borrow and do not repay, but the righteous show mercy and give.
medium.q: How do the wicked and the righteous differ concerning money?

medium.explanation: Verse 26 says, “His seed is blessed.”
medium.q: What is promised to the seed of the righteous?

answers: He will not give to others
He will not walk in the way
He will not remain helpless after falling
medium.explanation: The LORD upholds the fallen person with His hand.
medium.q: What does “not be utterly cast down” mean?

answers: Departing from evil and doing good are linked with dwelling for ever
Actions have no connection with stability
challenge.explanation: Verse 27 says, “Depart from evil, and do good; and dwell for evermore.”
challenge.q: What connection is made between doing good and stability?

answers: A testimony based on lifelong experience
A statement only about the future
challenge.explanation: The speaker appeals to what he has observed throughout life.
challenge.q: What does “I have been young, and now am old” contribute to the passage?

answers: It belongs only to the wicked
The righteous inherit and dwell in it for ever
challenge.explanation: The passage connects righteous living with enduring inheritance and dwelling.
challenge.q: How is inheriting the land connected with righteous conduct?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Person's Teaching and God's Protection

easy.explanation: Verse 30 says, “The mouth of the righteous speaketh wisdom.”
easy.q: What does the mouth of the righteous speak?

easy.explanation: Verse 31 says, “The law of his God is in his heart.”
easy.q: What is in the heart of the righteous person?

easy.explanation: The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to slay him.
easy.q: What does the wicked seek to do to the righteous?

answers: God's law is in his heart
medium.explanation: Because God's law is in his heart, none of his steps shall slide.
medium.q: Why are the steps of the righteous person firm?

answers: Wait on the LORD and keep His way
medium.explanation: Verse 34 commands, “Wait on the LORD, and keep his way.”
medium.q: What should a person do while waiting for God's help?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes steadfastness and spiritual stability.
medium.q: What does “none of his steps shall slide” mean?

answers: God's law in his heart shapes his wisdom and judgment
God's law makes him speak wicked schemes
challenge.explanation: He speaks wisdom and judgment because God's law is in his heart.
challenge.q: How are the righteous person's speech and God's law related?

answers: The wicked seek to kill, but the LORD does not abandon the righteous
The righteous seek to kill the wicked
challenge.explanation: The wicked pursue the righteous, while the LORD protects and judges him.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in this passage?

answers: Faith in God joined with a righteous life
challenge.explanation: The verse joins trusting expectation with faithful obedience.
challenge.q: What does “wait on the LORD” together with “keep his way” require?

paragraphs.title: The End of the Wicked and the Salvation of the Righteous

answers: Powerful and spreading like a green bay tree
easy.explanation: The psalm describes the wicked as being in great power and spreading like a green bay tree.
easy.q: How does the wicked man appear at first?

answers: He passed away and could not be found
easy.explanation: The speaker sought him, but he was no longer there.
easy.q: What happened to the wicked man afterward?

easy.explanation: The LORD is their strength in the time of trouble.
easy.q: Who is the strength of the righteous in trouble?

answers: The peaceable man has a future, but the wicked's end is cut off
The wicked have peace and the peaceable man has no future
medium.explanation: The upright man's end is peace, while the wicked's end is destruction.
medium.q: What is the difference between the end of the peaceable man and the end of transgressors?

medium.explanation: The final verse says the LORD helps, delivers, and saves them.
medium.q: What does the LORD do for the righteous?

answers: An appearance of strength and flourishing
medium.explanation: The wicked appears powerful and well established, though he later disappears.
medium.q: What does the image of the green bay tree emphasize?

answers: An impressive appearance does not guarantee lasting existence
challenge.explanation: Even a wicked person who seems deeply rooted may suddenly pass away.
challenge.q: What does the change from a powerful tree to disappearance teach?

answers: Mark the perfect man and behold the upright
challenge.explanation: Verse 37 tells the reader to mark the perfect and upright person.
challenge.q: What practical command accompanies hope in the LORD?

answers: He is their strength, helper, deliverer, and saviour
challenge.explanation: The final verses gather these descriptions of God's protection and salvation.
challenge.q: How does the conclusion summarize God's role toward the righteous?
